jobs.description:
SAFY is seeking a full time Case Manager I
for our Columbus
division in Ohio.

As a Case Manager I,
you will be responsible for the case management functions of a caseload of foster youth and homes. Works closely with youth, family, foster parents and community partners by equipping the youth and foster parents with the support and resources needed.

Who We Are

At SAFY, our mission is Preserving Families & Securing Futures. For 40 years, our work has rested on a single, radical idea – children belong in families. We believe that every child and family deserve the opportunity to reach their full potential. We are a team of 500 employees across seven states providing services such as Family Preservation & Reunification, Behavioral Health, Therapeutic Foster Care, Adoption Services and Older Youth Services so the families and children we serve can build resilience and thrive.

What You’ll Do

Travel daily to provide in-home, community-based services to families and youth in caseload.
Complete referral reviews and intake assignments. Communicate service availability to all assigned clients.
Provide instruction, intervention, and assistance as deemed necessary through the exercise of independent judgment and knowledge or as part of the treatment team to preserve the family unit.
Coordinate with county agency as appropriate and attend family sessions to promote successful clinical interventions with foster youth.
Build and maintain relationships with families and external case managers.
Coordinate and monitor service provisions for youth and family in the community and with school officials, courts and other appropriate parties involved with the client. This may include but is not limited to mental health, medical, educational, psychological, vocational and social services.
Develop and ensure completion of appropriate assessments including but not limited to Individualized Treatment Plans, Psychosocial Diagnostic Assessments (PSDs), and Mental Health Services Plans according to established time frames involving all appropriate parties as required by policy and regulations of the state and/or contract.
Timely document outcome of home visits, support sessions, safety assessments, interaction with parties involved in the youth's care and incident reports as required by policy, regulations, and contract requirements.
Ensure foster parents, youth and case manager needs are met during periods of staff transition.
May require rotating on-call schedule.
Participate in performance quality improvement process and execute any assigned tasks.
Successful completion of all required training pertaining to job.
Establish and maintain a positive working relationship, sensitive and responsive to the cultural differences with all levels of SAFY staff, clients, families and vendors.
Ability to work nontraditional hours daily/weekly to fulfill position duties; may include nights and/or weekends.
Ability to maintain confidential and sensitive information.
Complete Quarterly Environmental Audits (F-63) for all assigned Foster Homes.
Will conduct annual Foster Parent evaluations for Homes without youth.
Complete Home Studies or Amendments as required and collect all paperwork needed for foster home moves and/or the addition of new household members.
Amendments are required for all moves into or out of the foster home; when new Household members enter the home, etc.) All Home Study Amendments are approved and signed off by the Lead Licensing Specialist.
May complete Rules Investigations of all foster homes assigned by Lead LS or TD.
Completion of the Large Family Assessment (the state required assessment if a Foster to Adopt home has 5 or more youth).
Collect all documentation pertaining to licensing of applicants & Foster Parents.
Other duties or special projects as assigned.

What You Bring

We are looking for people from diverse backgrounds and experiences who are inspired by our noble mission to make a difference in the lives of the children and families in our care. You’ll be right at home if you are willing to learn from successes as well as setbacks, persevere in challenges and adversity, cultivate collaborative relationships, understand and leverage diversity, advocate for equity, aspire to work inclusively, and partner to drive your work and that of your team to the next level.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in the field of social work, counseling, psychology, sociology, child and family studies, or other approved related field of human services.
LSW, LPC or License Eligible preferred.
Two years of relevant experience with above listed degrees, experience in child welfare preferred, OR relevant experience in working with children in general.
Must have a valid driver’s license, acceptable driving record and auto insurance coverage to meet travel requirements; may require transporting youth if needed.

What We Offer

Targeted hiring range: $44,000.00 to $53,000.00
Compensation is commensurate with transferrable experience, education and licensure of candidate, location of the position, along with internal equity and budgeted amount for the role.

Comprehensive benefit plan options including Medical, Dental, Vision, Disability, Life Insurance, Flexible Spending and Health Savings account options to meet your needs

12 paid holidays per year, generous sick & vacation time and an additional day off for your birthday
All regular full and part time staff are eligible for quarterly and/or annual bonuses
Tuition Reimbursement up to $5,000 each year

jobs.title: Community Engagement Program Manager
jobs.description:
brighter NC (bNC) is a North Carolina-based public health and health justice focused organization committed to communities across North Carolina that have been overcriminalized and underserved by previous responses to drugs and drug use. Using a project-based approach, brighter NC is seeking to skill and build a statewide coalition of survivors who are dedicated to reducing the harmful impacts of drugs and drug use in their communities. 

Education and naloxone distribution have been proven to reduce overdose deaths in communities with the most access to these resources. Effective overdose prevention relies on intentional outreach and naloxone distribution in the communities that need them most. bNC is currently active in statewide overdose prevention efforts. Using principled frameworks, the Community Powered Overdose Prevention and Survival Awareness Campaign promotes overdose prevention and survival in underserved communities and to populations facing health disparities across the state. 

brighter NC is looking to hire a Community Engagement Program Manager to advance the goals of the campaign. Central to the Community Powered Overdose Prevention and Survival Awareness Campaign, this role will drive bNC’s efforts to reduce overdoses, improve health outcomes, and bridge health disparities by guiding a team of Specialized Community Health Workers and fostering intentional connections within communities. 

Leading brighter NC’s Outreach and Community Engagement Team, Community Engagement Program Manager will be responsible for:

Advancing bNC’s efforts to provide overdose prevention and outreach to communities across North Carolina with the greatest need. 
Steering the organization’s coalition efforts by leading the work to establish, nurture, maintain, and strengthen partnerships with service providers and other community-based organizations, and assisting with the planning of and guiding implementation of best-practice base-building. 
Liaising with bNC staff, directors, ambassadors, anchors, coalition members, and other key community and practice partners. 
Increasing visibility for the campaign and the organization, acting as the Community Powered Overdose Prevention and Survival Awareness Campaign’s foremost public relations representative.
Providing oversight and support to Specialized Community Health Workers and other outreach and engagement staff and volunteers and programming. 
Co-coordinating tabling, exhibiting, and vending at community and health-focused events.
Leading workshop, presentation, and outreach event coordination to enhance bNC’s community impact.
Co-developing and finalizing resource guides and other outreach materials. 
Co-creating work plans that advance professional and personal growth and development. 

Core Duties

Supervising Specialized Community Health Workers, and managing scheduling and coordination of continued implementation and expansion of community-based overdose prevention and survival outreach strategies proven to reduce the incidence of overdose, both fatal and non-fatal, prioritizing communities across the state with the greatest need. 
Guiding organization’s community engagement efforts. 
Tracking campaign metrics and engagement insights. 
Engaging with and staying connected to community anchors and organization ambassadors. 
Building networks to keep people connected, informed, and organized. 
Ensuring communities served are met right where they are, non-judgmentally and with warmth and positive regard. 

Experience

The ideal candidate for this role:
lives in North Carolina, 
is NC CHW certified or has over five years of experience working as a community health worker, 
has experience with project management or coordination, 
skilled at leading small teams, 
familiar with the harms associated with drug use, and knowledgeable about overdose prevention, syringe service programming and other strategies to reduce risks, and applying evidenced-based frameworks
comes to the role with lived experience and some community connections, 
has strong communication skills and experience with public speaking and presentations,
is comfortable traveling and providing outreach across the state, 
works well autonomously, and
is willing to work on weekends. 

Interested applicants:

Please send your current resume to work@brighternc.org

North Carolinians who have personal or familial experience with drug use, overdose, arrest, incarceration, sex work, HIV, Hepatitis C, disability, marginalization, or otherwise reflect the communities we serve are strongly encouraged to apply.

Du leder programmets samlede leverance og skaber et konstruktivt, resultatorienteret samarbejde mellem interne nøglepersoner og eksterne partnere. En vigtig del af opgaven er at omsætte kompleksitet til klare prioriteringer og et transparent beslutningsgrundlag for styregruppe og ledelse.

Etablere og drive programmets governance, organisering, arbejdsformer og beslutningsstruktur.
Udarbejde og vedligeholde den samlede programplan med scope, milepæle, ressourcer, budget og afhængigheder.
Lede ERP-programmet fra design og implementering til go-live, stabilisering og efterfølgende udrulning på tværs af sites og selskaber.
Styre og koordinere leverandører, implementeringspartnere og øvrige eksterne rådgivere, herunder opfølgning på kontrakter og leverancer.
Sikre sammenhæng mellem ERP og centrale platforme som MES, PLM og øvrige relevante IT- og OT-løsninger i tæt samarbejde med Group IT Manager.
Koordinere Business Process Owners, Master Data Management og Change Management ind i programmets planer og leverancer.

Forberede og drive styregruppemøder samt udarbejde beslutningsoplæg og præcis statusrapportering til ledelsen.
Sikre fokus på business case, gevinstrealisering og organisatorisk forankring gennem hele programmet.
Opbygge og udvikle et stærkt program- og projektteam med tydeligt ansvar, høj samarbejdsevne og en leveranceorienteret kultur.

SAFY is seeking a full time Case Manager I
for our Columbus
division in Ohio.

As a Case Manager I,
you will be responsible for the case management functions of a caseload of foster youth and homes. Works closely with youth, family, foster parents and community partners by equipping the youth and foster parents with the support and resources needed.

Who We Are

At SAFY, our mission is Preserving Families & Securing Futures. For 40 years, our work has rested on a single, radical idea – children belong in families. We believe that every child and family deserve the opportunity to reach their full potential. We are a team of 500 employees across seven states providing services such as Family Preservation & Reunification, Behavioral Health, Therapeutic Foster Care, Adoption Services and Older Youth Services so the families and children we serve can build resilience and thrive.

What You’ll Do

Travel daily to provide in-home, community-based services to families and youth in caseload.
Complete referral reviews and intake assignments. Communicate service availability to all assigned clients.
Provide instruction, intervention, and assistance as deemed necessary through the exercise of independent judgment and knowledge or as part of the treatment team to preserve the family unit.
Coordinate with county agency as appropriate and attend family sessions to promote successful clinical interventions with foster youth.
Build and maintain relationships with families and external case managers.
Coordinate and monitor service provisions for youth and family in the community and with school officials, courts and other appropriate parties involved with the client. This may include but is not limited to mental health, medical, educational, psychological, vocational and social services.
Develop and ensure completion of appropriate assessments including but not limited to Individualized Treatment Plans, Psychosocial Diagnostic Assessments (PSDs), and Mental Health Services Plans according to established time frames involving all appropriate parties as required by policy and regulations of the state and/or contract.
Timely document outcome of home visits, support sessions, safety assessments, interaction with parties involved in the youth's care and incident reports as required by policy, regulations, and contract requirements.
Ensure foster parents, youth and case manager needs are met during periods of staff transition.
May require rotating on-call schedule.
Participate in performance quality improvement process and execute any assigned tasks.
Successful completion of all required training pertaining to job.
Establish and maintain a positive working relationship, sensitive and responsive to the cultural differences with all levels of SAFY staff, clients, families and vendors.
Ability to work nontraditional hours daily/weekly to fulfill position duties; may include nights and/or weekends.
Ability to maintain confidential and sensitive information.
Complete Quarterly Environmental Audits (F-63) for all assigned Foster Homes.

Oplysning Om Indsamling Af Dine Personoplysninger

Ved udfyldelse af spørgeskemaet indhentes oplysninger om dit navn, e-mail, køn, CV og ansøgning.

Vi behandler de personoplysninger, du har afgivet i dette spørgeskema. Formålet med ovennævnte behandling af dine personoplysninger er en vurdering af dine kompetencer i forhold til det konkrete opslag hos virksomheden/organisationen, du har søgt ansættelse hos, samt i forhold til fremtidige stillinger.

Dine oplysninger i dette spørgeskema kan blive omfattet af en automatisk afgørelse, herunder profilering. Logikken bag denne afgørelse er brug af saglige kriterier, som gør det muligt at finde frem til de registrerede, som har de kompetencer, som søges til den pågældende stilling.

Som led i vurderingen kan dine dokumenter (fx CV og ansøgning) blive analyseret ved hjælp af kunstig intelligens (AI) med det formål at generere indsigter til brug for vurderingen. AI-analysen anvendes som støtte og træffer ikke selvstændige afgørelser - den endelige vurdering foretages altid med menneskelig involvering. Behandlingen kan indebære overførsel af dine oplysninger til tredjelande uden for EU/EØS, som sker på grundlag af EU-Kommissionens standardkontraktsbestemmelser (SCC) og/eller EU-US Data Privacy Framework. Du kan få oplyst det nærmere overførselsgrundlag ved henvendelse til den dataansvarlige.

Behandlingen af dine personoplysninger er baseret på dit samtykke.

Dit samtykke til de ovennævnte behandlinger af dine oplysninger kan til enhver tid tilbagekaldes med det resultat, at registreringen af oplysningerne slettes. Tilbagekaldelse kan ske ved henvendelse til den dataansvarlige.

Dine personoplysninger vil blive opbevaret i en periode på 6 måneder og derefter slettet.

Det er frivilligt at besvare de stillede spørgsmål, men undlader du at besvare spørgsmålene, bevirker det, at den dataansvarlige ikke vil være i stand til at vurdere din kompetence på den forudsatte måde.

PROGRAM MANAGER - ERP TRANSFORMATION

Vil du være med til at drive en af de mest betydningsfulde digitale transformationer i BIRN Groups historie?

BIRN Group står foran implementeringen af en ny fælles ERP-platform på tværs af koncernens selskaber og forretningsområder. Samtidig skal centrale platforme og processer omkring blandt andet produktion, produktdata og master data hænge sammen med ERP-løsningen og understøtte virksomhedens behov.

Derfor søger vi nu en erfaren Program Manager, der kan sikre følgeskab, eksekvere og tage det samlede ansvar for transformationen og føre organisationen sikkert fra beslutning og design til implementering, go-live og stabil drift.

Som Program Manager får du det overordnede ansvar for at etablere og drive BIRN Groups ERP-program. Du skaber struktur, fremdrift og tydelige beslutningsveje på tværs af arbejdsprocesser, selskaber og fagområder. Du sikrer samtidig, at mennesker, processer, data og teknologi tænkes sammen, så programmet skaber varige forretningsmæssige forbedringer.

Du leder programmets samlede leverance og skaber et konstruktivt, resultatorienteret samarbejde mellem interne nøglepersoner og eksterne partnere. En vigtig del af opgaven er at omsætte kompleksitet til klare prioriteringer og et transparent beslutningsgrundlag for styregruppe og ledelse.

Etablere og drive programmets governance, organisering, arbejdsformer og beslutningsstruktur.
Udarbejde og vedligeholde den samlede programplan med scope, milepæle, ressourcer, budget og afhængigheder.
Lede ERP-programmet fra design og implementering til go-live, stabilisering og efterfølgende udrulning på tværs af sites og selskaber.
Styre og koordinere leverandører, implementeringspartnere og øvrige eksterne rådgivere, herunder opfølgning på kontrakter og leverancer.
Sikre sammenhæng mellem ERP og centrale platforme som MES, PLM og øvrige relevante IT- og OT-løsninger i tæt samarbejde med Group IT Manager.
Koordinere Business Process Owners, Master Data Management og Change Management ind i programmets planer og leverancer.

Opbygge og udvikle et stærkt program- og projektteam med tydeligt ansvar, høj samarbejdsevne og en leveranceorienteret kultur.

Dokumenteret erfaring med Programme Management og større ERP-implementeringer, gerne end-to-end fra design til stabil drift.
Erfaring med multi-site eller international rollout og koordinering på tværs af selskaber, geografier og forretningsenheder.
God forståelse for centrale forretningsprocesser inden for eksempelvis økonomi, indkøb, salg, produktion, logistik og supply chain.

As a Social Worker
in the Ashfield North Family Support & Safeguarding Team, your role will be dynamic and rewarding. You will work with children of all ages, primarily completing child and family assessments for some of our most vulnerable children. Collaborating closely with the Multi-Agency Safeguarding Hub (MASH) and various agencies, you will identify needs and manage each child’s plan, aiming to foster positive change within their home environment. With the support of your Team Manager and colleagues, you will respond to identified risks and ensure the best outcomes for the children and families you serve. Don’t miss out on this opportunity to make a difference!

In This Role, You Will

Conduct thorough assessments of children and families to identify needs.
Collaborate with MASH and other agencies to develop effective support plans.
Monitor and review child protection plans to ensure safety and well-being.
Engage with families to provide support and guidance. Document all interactions and maintain accurate records in our internal database.
Attend meetings and contribute to multi-agency discussions to safeguard children.

To Succeed In This Role, You Will Need

A BA in Social Work or an equivalent qualification.
Registration with Social Work England.
A solid understanding of child development and family dynamics.
Experience in child protection and safeguarding practices.
Knowledge of relevant legislation, including the Children Act 1989/2004.

We Are Looking For Candidates Who Demonstrate

Compassionate Communication: Ability to engage effectively with children and families.
Collaborative Spirit: Willingness to work as part of a team and build positive relationships.
Analytical Thinking: Strong assessment and decision-making skills.
Resilience: Ability to manage challenging situations with professionalism and empathy.
